Verify deployment values for CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and AUTH_SESSION_DOMAIN: production CORS defaults to APP_URL but permits an environment override, and the session cookie domain is supplied at runtime. No deployed values were available in this source-only review.

Deployment-only verification remains useful: confirm the Discord application's registered callback URIs match the deployed DISCORD_REDIRECT_URI and INVITATION_ACCEPTANCE_DISCORD_REDIRECT_URI. Phoenix uses configured redirect URIs for both authorization and code exchange; provider registration is not visible in repository source.

The pricing preview intentionally distinguishes an invalid submitted promotion code from a valid one and returns that invitee's resulting price; source does not establish that promotion codes are confidential, so operational policy should not rely on their secrecy.

OnboardingController accepts caller-supplied mandateContext.ipAddress and userAgent in preference to request-derived values, and StripePayment forwards them as online mandate acceptance data. The source trace establishes caller control, but this review did not establish an unauthorized payment outcome or other security impact; consider deriving these values server-side.
The public invitation GET response is explicitly limited to id, status, invitation type, pricing tier, and expiry; its JSON renderer does not expose email, DOB, or names.

Waitlist registration validates person details before duplicate checks when registration is open, and the source tests assert that duplicate refusals have byte-identical accepted responses and do not persist replacement data. The possible timing channel remains unvalidated.

Stripe timestamp freshness enforces only a lower age bound, so far-future timestamps are not explicitly rejected. This is not a demonstrated vulnerability because producing such a timestamp still requires a valid Stripe HMAC; consider adding an upper skew bound as defense in depth.

DhcWeb.Router runs the :api pipeline before :intake_link, so an early :api halt (for example, a non-JSON unsafe request rejected by RequireJsonBody) can bypass the Intake plug's Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control headers. The rejection body is generic and no token disclosure or cache impact was demonstrated; if the header guarantee is intended to include pre-router/parser rejections, apply those static headers earlier in the endpoint pipeline.

The public /api/health endpoint is explicitly excluded from production force-SSL for Fly health checks, but its response contains only a static ok status. No sensitive status or configuration is exposed by the inspected controller.
Non-finding: GET /api/options is public, but its Members.options response contains only global gender and weapon enum labels; the insurance-form link is routed separately through authenticated_api.

The push endpoint validator permits non-default ports on allowlisted hosts. Consider restricting endpoints to HTTPS port 443 if browser-generated push subscriptions are the only supported input; the source review and bounded parser check did not establish an unintended-host impact.
Changed role assignments atomically revoke the target's session and socket tokens and disconnect established sockets; identical role submissions preserve tokens and do not disconnect.

EmailRefusals performs lock-free cross-table reads. Concurrent public Waitlist registration and direct invitation issue for the same email could each pass its refusal checks because the Waitlist and pending-Invitation unique indexes do not enforce a cross-table constraint. The source paths suggest a possible duplicate/inconsistent record outcome, but the invitation still requires members.invite authority and no unauthorized principal or disclosure was established, so this was not promoted as a security candidate.

The public external-checkout path accepts a returnUrl if it contains the CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID placeholder and forwards it to Stripe. No cross-principal impact is established from the Phoenix source alone; Stripe's return-URL restrictions were not assessed.

DoorView.load/2 hydrates roster and related personal fields before BeginnersWorkshopDoorController.show/2 checks the returned assignment resource. The controller does not render the view on denial, so no direct disclosure was established; consider checking assignment using a minimal resource read before loading the PII-bearing view.

IntakeEmails.Renderer.render_subject substitutes firstName without rejecting internal CR/LF/control characters. Waitlist registration trims the name and caps its length but does not reject internal line breaks; the email worker only checks that the subject is nonblank. The value is delivered to the registering person's own address, so this review found no cross-principal impact or confirmed header-injection behavior. Consider rejecting control characters after substitution.

The transactional email worker includes recipient email addresses in its logging context and validation-failure log metadata. This is PII in logs; source review did not establish an unauthorized log reader, so it is not reported as a vulnerability.

The offline eval has no file-size, row-count, or per-run provider-call limit. It is a caller-invoked operator CLI rather than a public endpoint; consider explicit operational caps to reduce accidental resource use on oversized exports.

A Web Push delivery or Intake Reply forward that already loaded its row may finish an external send concurrently with retention/deletion. The visible recipients remain the original notification subscriber or club inbox, so this review found no unauthorized reader; if the lifecycle contract is intended to cancel in-flight sends too, serialize delivery with deletion or recheck the durable row immediately before sending.

The Waitlist import parser reads the entire operator-selected file and materializes every record without visible file, row, or cell limits. Consider explicit import-size and row limits if operators may process externally supplied sheets; no remote import route or lower-trust automatic file selection was found.
The E2E harness key has a predictable test-only default. Keep E2E_SERVER restricted to test builds and the test listener loopback-only; do not expose a test-mode server through a deployment proxy.

Keep access to the Discord assignments Mix task restricted to trusted host operators: its principal ID arguments are audit actor selectors, while the service validates the selected principal's capability rather than authenticating the OS caller.

Discord Doctor's server-member cache retains provider roster data for up to 60 seconds; this is an explicit short cache window, and current application membership, roles, and kick eligibility are re-evaluated when building each report or kick.

Non-finding: container details expose each contained item ID and category summary to authenticated members by explicit ALE-106 route, controller, test, and OpenAPI contract. The separate member catalog withholds location for ordinary browsing; changing container-detail visibility would be a product/API policy change, not a missing authorization control established by this source review.

The member attempt and completion metadata remain bound to the authenticated principal; this review did not establish registration attribution takeover. The unresolved candidate concerns the separate Stripe Customer association and its provider-side effect.

Dockerfile.dev runs with the base image's default user and exposes port 4000. It is identified as a development image, and the assigned source does not establish its Compose mounts or network attachment; no host-boundary impact is demonstrated.
